steps.title: A named box
steps.say: A **variable** is a box with a name on it. You put a value in, and later you use the name to get the value back out. Here's one:

steps.title: The type
steps.say: First comes the **type**: what kind of value fits in the box. `int` holds whole numbers.

steps.title: The name
steps.say: Next, the **name**: how you'll refer to the box later. Pick one that says what it holds. Java names start lowercase, and each new word starts with a capital (`wheelCount`).

marks.label: name: how you use it later

steps.title: The value
steps.say: `=` means **put this value in the box**. It isn't "equals" like in math. It's an instruction.

marks.label: name: how you use it later

steps.title: The semicolon
steps.say: Every Java statement ends with a **semicolon**. Forgetting one is the most common build error, and the console will point right at it.

marks.label: name: how you use it later

steps.title: Four types you'll use most
steps.say: Different values need different types. These four cover almost everything at first.

steps.title: Changing what's in the box
steps.say: After a variable exists you can put a new value in it. You don't write the type again, because the box already exists. Java works out the right-hand side first, then stores the answer.

steps.title: Constants
steps.say: Some values should never change, like a robot's top speed. `final` locks the box, so the compiler stops anyone who tries to change it. Team standard: constants are named in `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`.

steps.title: Now in your code
steps.say: Let's find one in your own project. In the java-variables lesson it's `src/Main.java`.

steps.title: There it is
steps.say: That's a constant waiting for its value: type `String`, name `TEAM_NAME`, and an empty value `""`. Your task is to put the right text between the quotes.
